lines.content: This project uses Gradle for **build automation and dependency management**. **We recommend reading [this Gradle tutorial from se-edu/guides](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/gradle.html).**
The following commands perform common Gradle tasks.
* **`clean`**: Deletes the files created during the previous build tasks (e.g. files in the `build` folder).
* **`shadowJar`**: Uses the Shadow plugin to create the fat JAR file `build/libs/PolicyHarbor.jar`.
**`runShadow`**: Builds the application as a fat JAR, then runs it.
* **`checkstyleMain`**: Runs the code style check for the main code base.
**`checkstyleTest`**: Runs the code style check for the test code base.
* `./gradlew clean test`: Cleans the project before running all tests
This project uses GitHub Actions for CI. The necessary workflow configuration files are in `.github/workflows`. No further setup is required.
As part of CI, Gradle generates JaCoCo coverage reports from the tests, and CI uploads the coverage data to Codecov. Codecov then provides information about test coverage.
Coverage is evidence for investigating untested behavior, not a fixed release percentage. Check the workflow result and report-upload logs rather than assuming a green badge proves correctness.
To enable Codecov for forks of this project, follow the steps given in [this se-edu guide](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/codecov.html).

In addition to Gradle checks, CI runs repository-wide checks. Unlike Gradle checks, which cover files used in the build, these checks cover every repository file and enforce rules that are hard to apply on development machines, such as line-ending requirements.

These checks are implemented as POSIX shell scripts, and thus can only be run on POSIX-compliant operating systems such as macOS and Linux. To run all checks locally on these operating systems, execute the following in the repository root directory:
Any warnings or errors will be printed out to the console.

* Checks are implemented as executable `check-*` scripts within the `.github` directory. The `run-checks.sh` script will automatically pick up and run files named as such. That is, you can add more such files if you need and the CI will do the rest.
* Check scripts should print out errors in the format `SEVERITY:FILENAME:LINE: MESSAGE`
* SEVERITY is either ERROR or WARN.
* FILENAME is the path to the file relative to the current directory.
* LINE is the line of the file where the error occurred and MESSAGE is the message explaining the error.
* Check scripts must exit with a non-zero exit code if any errors occur.
Release from the tested team `master` commit. Do not upload a JAR built with a local OS-only dependency override.

**Published v1.5:** the [release](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/releases/tag/v1.5) uses [tag `v1.5`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/tree/v1.5) at `cb060cf3460df83499e9eea4ab9865d9ebe664c3`. Its asset is `PolicyHarbor.jar`; see the [published-artifact verification record](Testing.html#published-v15-verification). The procedure below applies to future releases; do not recreate or move the existing v1.5 tag.
1. Set `MainApp.VERSION` and the window title to the intended version; review branding, command documentation and `docs/images/Ui.png` against the product.
1. Use Java 25. On Mac, activate the [prescribed Zulu JDK+FX distribution](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html) for building and running.

1. Confirm that all intended release changes are merged into team `master`; record its full SHA and require successful Java CI on that exact commit. Run `./gradlew clean check coverage shadowJar`, then `.github/run-checks.sh` and `git diff --check` (Windows: `gradlew.bat`; repository shell checks run on macOS/Linux or CI). Keep audit evidence and other worktrees outside the build directory before using `clean`.

1. Copy `build/libs/PolicyHarbor.jar` into a fresh writable folder. From that folder run `java -jar PolicyHarbor.jar` and check the [manual workflow](DeveloperGuide.html#appendix-instructions-for-manual-testing), including save/restart. Also verify `java -ea -jar PolicyHarbor.jar`; assertions must not change validation or storage behavior. Keep synthetic screenshot data separate from personal data.

1. Inspect the existing product screenshot against the tested JAR. Retain `docs/images/Ui.png` if it still shows the real dashboard, permanent Client IDs and meaningful fictional clients; replace it only when the interface has changed. Verify the deployed homepage, User Guide, Developer Guide, About Us page and their links after Pages completes for the release commit.

1. Once publication is authorized, create the intended version tag at the exact tested commit in the team repository. [Create a GitHub release](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository) titled with the product name and intended version and attach `PolicyHarbor.jar`. A short description of changes since the previous release, Java 25 requirements, the User Guide link and known limitations is sufficient; detailed release notes are optional. Do not tag or publish while required checks, intended merges or artifact verification remain incomplete.
1. Download the uploaded JAR and verify startup. Compare its SHA-256 with the local artifact (`shasum -a 256 PolicyHarbor.jar` on Mac, `sha256sum` on Linux, or `Get-FileHash` in PowerShell).

1. After publishing, ensure completed issues/PRs are assigned to the iteration milestone, move any incomplete items to a later milestone, and close the completed milestone. Preserve PR source branches.
CI uses Zulu JDK+FX on Windows, macOS and Linux. CI builds/tests are useful evidence but do not replace running the exact uploaded JAR or checking its GUI.
title: Setting up and getting started
## Setting up the project on your computer
Follow the steps below precisely. The setup may fail if you skip or change a step.

First, **fork** the [team repository](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp), then **clone** your fork. Use Java 25 for Gradle and the IDE. **Mac users:** follow the [Zulu JDK+FX setup](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html); other distributions can fail to load the JavaFX native libraries.
If you plan to use IntelliJ IDEA (highly recommended):

1. **Configure the JDK**: Follow the guide [_[se-edu/guides] IDEA: Configuring the JDK_](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/intellijJdk.html) to ensure IntelliJ is configured to use **JDK 25**.

1. **Import the project as a Gradle project**: Follow the guide [_[se-edu/guides] IDEA: Importing a Gradle project_](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/intellijImportGradleProject.html) to import the project into IDEA.
:exclamation: Note: Importing a Gradle project is slightly different from importing a normal Java project.
1. Run `./gradlew run` and try a few commands. Gradle enables Java assertions for application runs, including `runShadow`, and tests.
1. [Run the tests](Testing.html) to ensure they all pass.

If you run `seedu.address.Main` directly through IntelliJ instead of Gradle, open **Run > Edit Configurations**, select the application configuration, choose **Modify options > Add VM options**, and enter `-ea`. Apply this to each application run configuration you use. See the [SE-EDU assertions instructions](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/intellijUsefulSettings.html#enabling-assertions). Keep personal IDE configurations out of Git.

Build the packaged application with `./gradlew shadowJar`. From the project root, run `java -ea -jar build/libs/PolicyHarbor.jar`; alternatively, change into the directory containing the JAR and run `java -ea -jar PolicyHarbor.jar`.

Packaged launches resolve `data/addressbook.json`, `preferences.json` and `.policyharbor.lock` relative to the JAR's folder, regardless of the working directory. With the JAR still in `build/libs`, both commands above use `build/libs/data/addressbook.json`. A symbolic link to the JAR uses the physical target JAR's folder.
Direct IDE launches and `./gradlew run` use their configured working directory, normally the project root. A packaged launch does not automatically import data from that development folder.

For manual checks, copy the JAR into a fresh writable folder outside `build/`, launch it from that folder and use fictional data. Changing only the working directory does not select a separate client file. Do not keep important records under `build/`: `./gradlew clean` removes that directory.

A direct `java -jar` launch does not inherit Gradle's assertion settings. Also check an ordinary launch without `-ea`, using the same JAR path: assertions protect internal programmer assumptions and must not replace user-input validation or file-error handling.
If using IDEA, follow the guide [_[se-edu/guides] IDEA: Configuring the code style_](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/intellijCodeStyle.html) to set up IDEA's coding style to match ours.

Optionally, follow the guide [_[se-edu/guides] Using Checkstyle_](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/checkstyle.html) to learn how to use Checkstyle in IDEA, for example to report problems _as_ you write code.
This project includes GitHub Actions configuration files in `.github/workflows`. GitHub runs CI automatically for every push and pull request. No setup is required.
When you are ready to start coding, we recommend that you get some sense of the overall design by reading about [PolicyHarbor’s architecture](DeveloperGuide.html#architecture).
These tutorials will help you get acquainted with the codebase.
Use Java 25; on Mac select the [prescribed Zulu JDK+FX](https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/javaInstallationMac.html) for both Gradle and the IDE.

On Windows use `gradlew.bat`. `check` runs the JUnit suite and Checkstyle. Reports are under `build/reports/tests/test`, `build/reports/checkstyle` and `build/reports/jacoco`. On macOS/Linux also run `.github/run-checks.sh` and `git diff --check`.
During development, run a focused class with:
A focused run does not establish whole-suite coverage. Run the full suite before reporting overall results. Use `clean` when stale build outputs are a concern; it is not required for every test run.
IntelliJ can run a class, package or `src/test/java` through its JUnit runner. Ensure its configured JDK matches Gradle's.

Gradle explicitly enables assertions for `Test` and `JavaExec` tasks, including `test`, `run` and `runShadow`. An assertion failure signals an internal invariant violation; investigate it rather than disabling assertions to make a check pass. Assertions must have no side effects and must not be the only validation for user input, external files or recoverable errors.

For a direct IntelliJ application launch, enable `-ea` in its VM options as described in [Setting up](SettingUp.html#setting-up-the-project-on-your-computer). Build the packaged application with `./gradlew shadowJar`. From the project root, run each command below separately, closing the application between runs:

For isolated manual checks, use a fresh writable folder with fictional data and specify the absolute path to the built JAR. If you copy the JAR into that folder, use `PolicyHarbor.jar` as the path instead. Both modes must preserve normal validation and save/load protection. The Gradle daemon's JVM arguments or a task dry run alone do not prove assertions are active in the application JVM.
| Unit | Domain constraints, parsers and pure display values | `FollowUpTest`, `ViewCommandParserTest`, `ClientProfilePanelTest` |
| Integration | Model transitions and cooperating components | `ClientProfileSelectionTest`, `LogicManagerTest`, `JsonAddressBookStorageTest` |
| Workflow | Real command routing, persistence, failure preservation and restart | `ClientRecordCommandsTest`, `ClientProfileWorkflowIntegrationTest` |

Tests use fixed dates and temporary data folders. Storage failure tests inject write/move failures rather than relying on OS permissions. Keep successful and rejected commands' data/view assertions together.

Pure display-function tests do not prove FXML binding, focus, wrapping or scaling. Follow the Developer Guide's [manual testing appendix](DeveloperGuide.html#appendix-instructions-for-manual-testing) against the actual JAR before a release, and record the tested platform/runtime and remaining gaps.

The [published v1.5 release](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/releases/tag/v1.5) uses [source tag `v1.5`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/tree/v1.5) at `cb060cf3460df83499e9eea4ab9865d9ebe664c3`. Its [PolicyHarbor.jar](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/releases/download/v1.5/PolicyHarbor.jar) is **12,587,362 bytes**, with SHA-256:

**Uploaded-asset check (29 October 2026):** the official download passed ZIP integrity and executable-manifest checks, matched GitHub's asset digest, and was byte-for-byte identical to the separately built artifact from the tagged source. In a fresh folder on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with Zulu JDK+FX 25.0.3, `java -jar PolicyHarbor.jar` started and displayed the native window title `PolicyHarbor v1.5`. The published binary was not rebuilt or replaced during this check.

The earlier comprehensive QA used source `97c10e2ad63e20b00db58657d5cd06182de0ae6f`, a **12,587,304-byte** JAR before the final invisible-only address fix in PR #249. That different candidate has SHA-256:

Retain its results as historical evidence, not as the final release checksum. This uploaded-asset check repeated startup and identity verification; it does not claim a new complete GUI regression, Windows/Linux desktop verification or completion of the physical display matrix. The alternate-working-directory file-location concern remains separate unresolved work.
## v1.5 dashboard layout and platform matrix

`DashboardLayoutBoundaryTest` lays out the real window at the logical sizes of the release display matrix and checks a 1,000-client table, long unbroken profile values and a full pending summary. `DisplayMatrixFixture` writes the matching 1,000-client data file for packaged-JAR checks. Run `./gradlew displayMatrixFixture --args="/absolute/path/to/fresh-folder yyyy-MM-dd"`; the folder must not already contain a client-data file. `DisplayMatrixFixtureTest` checks round-trip loading, the reference-date distribution and refusal to overwrite existing data. Use `./gradlew packagedBackendCheck --args="/absolute/path/to/another-fresh-folder"` for a self-checking 1,000-client workflow and backend timings against the built JAR. This does not exercise keyboard/mouse input or rendering. Record automated results and every packaged OS/resolution/scaling check in the [v1.5 platform matrix](testing/v1.5/platform-matrix.html); combinations nobody has run stay pending.

The [28 October composed-candidate record](testing/v1.5/platform-matrix.html#composed-candidate-record-28-october-2026) identifies the exact source and JAR, 624 passing tests, three locally excluded native-input tests, packaged backend timings and limited ordinary/`-ea` startup observations. Physical resolution/scaling and desktop interaction remain pending; #135 is not complete.

`DashboardIntegrationTest` exercises the real window, Logic and temporary JSON storage: filtered indices versus the global summary, canonical selection after pending reordering, clear/delete, failed-save preservation, explicit error recovery, published-date refresh, observer cleanup and logical layout sizes.

The shown-window focus test in `ResultDisplayTest` and the shown-window repeated-overflow test in `ErrorFeedbackLayoutTest` need an interactive desktop. The macOS Actions profile skips these two tests unless `POLICYHARBOR_NATIVE_UI_TESTS=true`: the hosted worker aborts with SIGABRT during native window interaction. Scene-level focus, input retention, layout, feedback selection and clipboard regressions still run on every CI platform. The offscreen overflow test retains scrollbar, complete-text scrolling, selection, focus and compact-recovery assertions at all three logical sizes, including on macOS Actions. A local check using that profile must report the two skipped tests explicitly. Native packaged-app interaction and the real OS/resolution/scaling matrix are separate evidence; logical scene-size checks do not prove display scaling.

The three Robot-based command-submission tests were retired after reproducible desktop-activation/input failures. `CommandSubmissionTest` retains scene-level Enter/Run/Tab-Space routing, logical focus, rejected-input retention and failed-save rollback/retry checks. These do not replace native keyboard/mouse coverage. Before release, use the packaged JAR to verify Enter, mouse Run and Tab/Space separately with a successful command, a parse error, an invalid client ID and a save failure in disposable data. Check exactly-once submission, clearing after success, retained input/data after failure, and typing immediately afterwards without clicking or requesting focus again. Record the JAR checksum, platform/runtime and actual outcome; historical automated counts/exclusions in the platform matrix remain records of those earlier runs.

The Help restoration regression checks `HelpWindow.focus()` on an unshown stage: it must clear a pre-set iconified state, retain the same stage and remain safe when repeated. It runs on every CI platform without a skip or desktop opt-in. A shown stage's iconified state is controlled by the OS window manager, so this regression does not assert synchronous native minimise/restore transitions. For desktop verification, open Help, minimise it, then reopen it through the Help menu and F1 separately; allow the desktop to settle and confirm that the same window is restored and focused. The component regression does not prove that native interaction. See the [JavaFX Stage iconification contract](https://openjfx.io/javadoc/17/javafx.graphics/javafx/stage/Stage.html#iconifiedProperty()).

See the [Developer Guide's dashboard procedure](DeveloperGuide.html#integrated-v14-dashboard-checks) for manual acceptance and the [v1.4 release notes](releases/v1.4.html) for the user-visible increment.
Evidence is recorded by source revision; checks on an earlier packaged app do not establish the same coverage for the final JAR.

- **Integration baseline `ffda0137`:** packaged checks passed on macOS arm64 with Zulu 25+FX for ordinary and assertion-enabled startup, Enter/Run, typing after a rejected command, recovery, filtered table with the global pending summary, F1/Escape and save/restart. The product screenshots were captured from this packaged app.

- **Pre-release audit `9aced71d345fdbd6c9a5de59b81a121b86d36d0a` (21 October 2026):** fresh startup, add via Enter, follow-up via Run, profile selection, filtered table versus global summary, invalid-index input/focus retention, typing recovery, pending mode, F1/Escape and save/restart passed. Restart with `-ea` preserved saved clients/actions and reset selection; validation and recovery also passed. Saved bytes remained unchanged across restart and read-only commands.

- **Final v1.4 `28ed61635311779743324517bcdce154102cce39` (21 October 2026):** fresh packaged startup and `list` passed. The broader GUI scenarios above, assertion-enabled launch and save/restart were not repeated against this final JAR.

The pre-release audit and final smoke check used macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64, with Zulu JDK+FX 25.0.3+9-LTS (Zulu25.34+17-CA). Physical resolution/scaling was not recorded, so these runs do not establish the display matrix below.
The [published v1.4 release](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/releases/tag/v1.4) identifies the final source revision above. Its `PolicyHarbor.jar` is 12,558,262 bytes with SHA-256:
GitHub's reported asset digest matches the locally built JAR used for the final smoke check. Downloading and relaunching the uploaded asset was not separately verified.

On that final source, `check coverage shadowJar` passed locally using the committed macOS Actions test profile through a temporary init script: 576 tests, 572 passed and the four native desktop tests present at that revision skipped. Checkstyle, coverage generation and JAR packaging passed. [CI run 39600670010](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-W13-3/tp/actions/runs/39600670010) passed on Linux, macOS and Windows for the same source revision. These automated checks are separate from packaged desktop verification.

When adding verification evidence, record the exact source commit, JAR SHA-256, OS/JDK, actual resolution/scaling, date, result and evidence for each exercised case. Keep unavailable combinations explicitly pending rather than treating publication, a screenshot or green CI as proof.
// Positioning context for the mobile navigation icon
// Native details/summary: focusable, toggled by Enter/Space and announced as expanded/collapsed
// Gaps between nav items, but not on the last one

- **A light dashboard for daily client work.** A branded header, command bar, numbered client table and independently scrollable profile/follow-up panels replace the previous workspace. Drag the main and sidebar dividers to allocate space.

- **All pending actions stay visible while searching.** The new unnumbered sidebar includes every client's pending action, grouped into Overdue, Due Today and Upcoming. Filtering the table does not hide other clients' upcoming work. Each card includes the full action and due date.

- **A compact client table with safe command indices.** Names and contact values wrap; pending mode adds due-date and status columns. Sorting is disabled so displayed row numbers always match `view`, `delete` and `followup`. Narrow tables scroll horizontally.

- **A clearer selected-client profile.** Contact fields, sorted tag chips and the next follow-up appear in a light card. VIEWING markers follow the selected record across follow-up reordering, including clients who share a name.
- **Run commands with Enter or Run.** Both use the same submission path. Failed commands retain their input and restore typing focus; successful commands clear it.

- **Readable success and error feedback.** A compact, read-only strip wraps and scrolls complete messages. Errors have a text label as well as color; the next successful command clears the error state. The saved-data warning remains separate and persistent.
- **Refreshed Help and data-file information.** Help offers a selectable guide link, a Copy link button and Escape-to-close. The footer exposes long data paths in a wrapped tooltip.

- **Integrated regression protection.** Tests cover the complete feed, stable pending projection, view/selection consistency, save-failure isolation, date refresh and window cleanup. Developer runs and tests enable assertions without requiring users to launch with them.

- **Safer saved-data loading.** JSON files with trailing non-whitespace content or additional root values are rejected instead of partially accepted. Invalid saved client data starts a protected session that blocks changes and preserves the original file.
- **More reliable email validation.** Iterative character scanning preserves the supported client email formats while avoiding stack overflow on unusually long inputs.
The existing seven commands and local JSON format are preserved. Each client still has one pending action; multiple actions, history, notifications and typed contact editing are outside this release.

This page records v1.5 dashboard usability evidence: automated layout boundaries and packaged-JAR checks on real desktops. Logical scene sizes in automated tests are not evidence of physical display scaling, font substitution or OS window behaviour; a combination counts as checked only after someone runs the packaged JAR on it.

`DashboardLayoutBoundaryTest` composes the real `MainWindow` over temporary storage and lays it out at 853x480, 1536x864 and 1920x1080 logical pixels, which correspond to 1280x720 at 150%, 1920x1080 at 125% and 1920x1080 at 100%.

The table describes the current source assertions, not a new test run.

Already covered elsewhere, so not repeated: restored window geometry extremes (`DashboardShellTest.getWindowBounds_*`), recycled table rows (`PersonListPanelTest`), narrow-table horizontal scrolling (`PersonListPanelTest.narrowWidth_columnsDoNotFit_scrollsHorizontally`), long tags (`ClientProfilePanelTest`) and long feedback (`ResultDisplayTest`).
The wrapping tests were checked against a regression: turning off wrapping on the profile email and on the pending action makes them fail with an ellipsis-clipped value.

**Historical row-index regression:** the original `table_thousandClients_lastIndexStaysReadable` checked row 1000 (rendered as `1...` before its fix) and a five-digit index in a 56 px `#` column. The current permanent-ID test above supersedes that reference; the dated run below describes the earlier source.

**Run record (27 October 2026):** macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64, Homebrew OpenJDK 25.0.5.0.2. This machine has no Zulu JDK+FX, so the project's x86_64 JavaFX 17.0.7 natives could not load; the run supplied the official arm64 JavaFX 17.0.7 natives through `-Djava.library.path`. Source: uncommitted working tree on top of `81c4d65f`; repeat on the final commit. All four boundary tests and Checkstyle passed. In the full suite, only the three native-input tests in `CommandSubmissionTest` failed, because this terminal cannot send native keyboard/mouse input; they fail identically without this change.

**Observation:** at 853x480 the pending summary's viewport is about 99 px tall, shorter than one 114 px card. Scrolling still reaches every card, and the sidebar divider gives the summary more room. This is not treated as a defect, but screenshots and manual checks at 1280x720/150% should expect it.

**Fixture safety and repeatability.** `DisplayMatrixFixtureTest` invokes the actual generator with an explicit date, reloads all 1,000 records through storage, checks the 29 overdue / 2 due-today / 70 upcoming distribution and long values, and verifies that regeneration refuses to overwrite existing data.

The existing layout changes and documentation from PR #136 are merged. This follow-up adds repeatable fixture generation and a packaged backend check; it does **not** complete the physical display matrix.

- **Source:** [fb0a548cc69a61a9c99110c099ff1b4137d74e41](https://github.com/wkc75/tp/commit/fb0a548cc69a61a9c99110c099ff1b4137d74e41), a separate composed candidate containing the fixes for #130–#134 and these verification tools. This is not a merged release candidate on team master.
- **Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64; Zulu JDK+FX 25.0.3+9-LTS (Zulu25.34+17-CA); reference date 2026-10-28. Physical resolution/scaling was not verified.

- **Automated checks:** 624 tests passed, plus Checkstyle, coverage generation, the repository checks and packaging. Three native-input methods in `CommandSubmissionTest` were excluded locally: `submit_enterKey_submitsOnceAndRestoresTypingAfterSuccessAndFailure`, `submit_mouseClick_submitsOnceAndRestoresTypingAfterSuccessAndFailure`, and `submit_tabAndSpace_submitsOnceAndRestoresTypingAfterSuccessAndFailure`. All three failed the unchanged baseline because the initial native click did not reach the input. The exclusion is local; the committed CI configuration is unchanged.

- **Packaged backend:** `packagedBackendCheck` passed against production classes from this JAR with assertions enabled and 1,000 fictional clients. Filtering/index mapping, long-profile data, invalid-index rejection, follow-up reorder/clear/delete and save/reload passed. Selection was empty after reload.

- **Startup smoke only:** both ordinary `java -jar` and `java -ea -jar` launches loaded the fixture and reached UI startup without a fatal exception. The assertion-enabled launch left the data file byte-identical (SHA-256 `054d808d606109ae21510acf2be2337c3d504e47b36ab7905fc789e3cb0ef125`). The session could not inspect or interact with the Java window, so these are log/process observations, not proof of visual layout, Enter/Run, error focus recovery or scrolling. Each launch was stopped after the smoke check.
Single-run backend observations, measured inside `packagedBackendCheck` (including disk persistence for mutations):
| Replace the first action and reorder it to the end | 238.268 |
| Delete the first remaining pending client | 220.864 |
